extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agency staff (State plan authors) and affected EGU owners/operators preparing or implementing State plans to meet EPA emission guidelines for affected electric generating units (EGUs)
extracted.subtask_short: State plan for EGU CO2 standards
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a State plan to implement the EPA emission guidelines for affected steam-generating EGUs, including selecting and documenting standards of performance, monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting, applicability, and compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of standard of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard of performance for an affected EGU may take the following forms: (1) A rate-based standard of performance for an individual affected EGU that does not exceed the level calculated through the use of the methods described in § 60.5775b(c) and (d). (2) A standard of performance in an alternate form, which may apply for affected EGUs in the long-term coal-fired steam generating unit subcategory or the medium-term coal-fired steam generating unit subcategory, as provided for in § 60.5775b(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must select one of these forms for each affected EGU and ensure the chosen form meets all other requirements in the subpart (quantifiable, verifiable, non-duplicative, permanent, enforceable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be quantifiable, verifiable, non-duplicative, permanent, and enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard(s) of performance for affected EGUs included under your State plan must be demonstrated to be quantifiable, verifiable, non-duplicative, permanent, and enforceable with respect to each affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State plan submittal must include the methods by which each standard meets each requirement: (1) Quantifiable: reliably measured in a manner that can be replicated. (2) Verifiable: adequate monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting to enable independent evaluation. (3) Non-duplicative: not already incorporated as a standard in the State plan. (4) Permanent: must be met continuously unless replaced by an approved revision. (5) Enforceable: (i) technically accurate limitation and time period specified; (ii) compliance requirements clearly defined; (iii) affected EGUs responsible and liable; (iv) each compliance activity enforceable as practical matter per 40 CFR 49.167; (v) Administrator, State, and third parties maintain ability to enforce and secure corrective actions (cites CAA sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal-fired steam generating units — BSER, degree, presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is CCS with 90 percent capture of CO2. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an emission rate limit defined by an 88.4 percent reduction in annual emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross) from the unit-specific baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may adopt the presumptively approvable standard or develop an alternate standard consistent with other provisions; baselines and calculations use unit-specific data per § 60.5775b(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal-fired steam generating units — BSER, degree, presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is natural gas co-firing at 40 percent of the heat input to the unit. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an emission rate limit defined by a 16 percent reduction in annual emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross) from the unit-specific baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preexisting co-firing is reflected in the baseline, States must account for it by adjusting the degree of emission limitation (example: 10% preexisting co-firing reduces required incremental reduction to 12%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base load oil-fired steam generating units — BSER and presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For base load oil-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an annual emission rate limit of 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may use this presumptively approvable standard for base load oil-fired units unless proposing alternate standards with required demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate load oil-fired steam generating units — BSER and presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For intermediate load oil-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an annual emission rate limit of 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same note: States can adopt presumptively approvable limits or propose alternates with required demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low load oil-fired steam generating units — BSER and presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For low load oil-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is uniform fuels. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is 170 lb CO2/MMBtu. (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an annual emission rate limit of 170 lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to the low load oil-fired subcategory; States must use the methods in (c) and (d) to determine baseline and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base load natural gas-fired steam generating units — BSER and presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For base load natural gas-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an annual emission rate limit of 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same structure as other subcategories; baseline and unit-specific calculations required per (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate load natural gas-fired steam generating units — BSER and presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For intermediate load natural gas-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an annual emission rate limit of 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply baseline and calculation methodologies in (d) to determine unit-specific values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low load natural gas-fired steam generating units — BSER and presumptively approvable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For low load natural gas-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is uniform fuels. (ii) Degree of emission limitation is 130 lb CO2/MMBtu. (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an annual emission rate limit of 130 lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As above, States may adopt these presumptively approvable standards or propose alternates with required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-specific baseline methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: A State shall use the CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation or, for affected EGUs in the low load oil- or natural gas-fired subcategory, heat input data for a given affected EGU from the most representative continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to May 9, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the continuous 8 quarters, divide total CO2 emissions (pounds) by total gross electricity generation (MWh) or by total heat input (MMBtu) for low-load subcategories to calculate baseline CO2 emission performance in lb CO2/MWh or lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate form — aggregate rate-based standard (owner/operator group)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include an aggregate rate-based standard (lb CO2/MWh-gross) that applies for a group of affected EGUs that share the same owner or operator, calculated on a gross generation weighted average basis, provided the standard meets the requirements of paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using an aggregate rate-based standard, the State plan must include specific documentation and demonstrate equivalent or better emission reductions (see paragraph (f) requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for aggregate rate-based standards (paragraph f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a State plan includes an aggregate rate-based standard for a group of EGUs sharing the same owner/operator, the plan must include: (1) the presumptively approvable rate-based standard for each affected EGU; (2) documentation of assumptions underlying the aggregate calculation; (3) process for calculating the aggregate gross generation weighted average emission rate at the end of each compliance period; (4) measures to implement and enforce the annual aggregate standard including basis for determining owner/operator compliance and provisions for ownership changes; (5) demonstration that the aggregate application achieves equivalent or better emission reduction as individual rate-based application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must provide transparent methods, assumptions, and enforcement approaches so equivalency can be independently evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate form — mass-based annual limit for individual EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include a mass-based standard in the form of an annual limit on allowable mass CO2 emissions for an individual affected EGU, provided the standard meets the requirements of paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass-based individual limits must meet documentation, utilization, enforcement, and equivalency demonstration requirements in (g), and include a backstop rate-based requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for individual mass-based limits (paragraph g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a State plan includes an annual mass CO2 limit for an individual EGU, the plan must include: (1) the presumptively approvable rate-based standard that would apply; (2) the utilization level used to calculate the mass limit with underlying data and assumptions; (3) measures to implement and enforce the annual limit, addressing assurance of equivalent performance; (4) a demonstration of equivalent or better emission reduction compared to the rate-based standard; (5) the backstop rate-based emission rate requirement applied annually; (6) special option for long-term coal-fired units to use a presumptively approvable mass limit equal to the rate-based standard × utilization corresponding to 80% capacity factor with a backstop equivalent to 80% reduction in baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must include data and justification for utilization assumptions and specify backstop procedures to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate form — rate-based standard implemented via rate-based emission trading (paragraph h)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State plan may implement a rate-based standard through a rate-based emission trading program where EGUs meet specified lb CO2/MWh rates and may surrender compliance instruments denoted in 1 short ton CO2 to adjust reported rates, provided the standard meets paragraph (h) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans using rate-based trading must include: presumptively approvable rate-based standards for participating EGUs; measures to implement and enforce the trading program including basis for awarding compliance instruments and the process for demonstrating compliance and surrendering instruments; and a demonstration of equivalent or better emission reduction than individual rate-based application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate form — mass-based standard implemented via mass-based CO2 trading (paragraph i)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State plan may implement a mass-based standard via a mass-based CO2 emission trading program where EGUs surrender allowances equal to reported mass CO2 emissions, provided the plan meets paragraph (i) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must include: presumptively approvable rate-based standards for participating EGUs; calculation of each EGU's mass CO2 budget contribution using assumed utilization and underlying data; measures to implement and enforce the annual budget and assurance of equivalent performance; demonstration of equivalent or better emission performance than individual rate-based application; and a backstop rate-based emission rate requirement for participating EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability-based relief documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply a less stringent standard or longer compliance schedule based on electric grid reliability (including resource adequacy) under § 60.24a(e)-(h), a State must provide with its State plan submission: (1) an analysis demonstrating the EGU is critical to maintaining electric reliability and projection of the period it's reliability critical; (2) analysis by the relevant reliability planning authority corroborating the asserted reliability risk and confirming the period of criticality; (3) a certification from the relevant authority that the reliability claims are accurate and the identified reliability problem requires the requested relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrations must show that requiring compliance would trigger non-compliance with mandatory FERC-approved reliability standards or increase loss of load expectation beyond regional targets; analyses must substantiate time period for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates and compliance periods
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include compliance dates: (a)(1) long-term coal-fired subcategory must require compliance starting no later than January 1, 2032 unless later date approved under § 60.24a(e)-(h); (a)(2) medium-term coal and various oil/natural-gas subcategories must require compliance starting no later than January 1, 2030 unless later date approved. (b) State plan must require EGUs to achieve compliance for each compliance period as defined in § 60.5880b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may request later dates under reliability provisions, but must document and justify such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements for State plan submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a State plan or a negative declaration letter with the information required under § 60.5740b by May 11, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All information required must be submitted according to electronic reporting requirements in § 60.5875b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for revising an EPA-approved State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA-approved State plans can be revised only with approval by the Administrator. The Administrator will approve a revision if it is satisfactory with respect to the applicable requirements of this subpart and all applicable requirements of subpart Ba. If one or more State plan elements in § 60.5740b require revision, the State must submit a revision pursuant to § 60.28a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions must be documented and demonstrate continued compliance with the subpart and procedural requirements for submission and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA commitment to review emission guidelines for coal-fired EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will review and, if appropriate, revise these emission guidelines as they apply to coal-fired steam generating affected EGUs by January 1, 2041, unless the Administrator determines review is not appropriate in light of readily available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a categorical commitment to reassess appropriateness of guidelines for coal-fired subcategories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to EGU owners/operators and federal backstop
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart does not directly affect EGU owners/operators in your State except as provided in § 60.5710b(b); however, affected EGU owners/operators must comply with the State plan. If a State does not submit a State plan by May 11, 2026, or EPA disapproves the plan, EPA will implement and enforce a Federal plan applicable to each affected EGU within the State (§ 60.5720b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should follow their State plan when adopted; otherwise federal plan obligations will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGUs that must be addressed and definition of affected EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: EGUs to be addressed: (a)(1) any affected EGUs that were in operation or had commenced construction on or before January 8, 2014; (a)(2) coal-fired steam generating units that commenced a modification on or before May 23, 2023. An affected EGU is a steam generating unit that: (1) serves a generator capable of selling greater than 25 MW to a utility power distribution system; and (2) has a base load rating greater than 260 GJ/hr (250 MMBtu/hr) heat input of fossil fuel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must identify units meeting these criteria and treat them as affected EGUs for plan obligations, except as excluded under § 60.5850b.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGUs excluded from being affected EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: EGUs excluded include: (a) new/reconstructed units subject to subpart TTTT due to commencing construction after subpart TTTT applicability date; (b) modified natural gas- or oil-fired units subject to subpart TTTT due to modification date; (c) modified coal-fired units subject to subpart TTTTa due to modification date; (d) units subject to federally enforceable permit limiting net-electric sales to one-third or less (or ≤219,000 MWh) and never exceeded that limit; (e) non-fossil fuel units able to derive ≥50% heat input from non-fossil fuel with permit limiting fossil fuel use to ≤10% annual capacity factor; (f) CHP units with permit limiting annual net-electric sales to ≤219,000 MWh or product of design efficiency and potential output; (g) units that serve a generator along with other EGUs where prorated effective generation capacity ≤25 MW; (h) municipal waste combustors subject to 40 CFR part 60 subpart Eb; (i) commercial/industrial solid waste incineration units subject to subpart CCCC; (j) EGUs deriving >50% heat input from an industrial process that does not produce electrical/mechanical output or useful thermal output used outside the EGU; (k) existing coal-fired units that have demonstrated plans to permanently cease operations before Jan 1, 2032 pursuant to § 60.5740b(a)(9)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must evaluate each candidate unit against this exclusion list when determining affected EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan requirement (40 CFR 75.53(g),(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator of an affected EGU required to meet standards must prepare a monitoring plan in accordance with applicable provisions in 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h), unless such a plan is already in place under another program that requires CO2 mass emissions to be monitored and reported according to 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plans must meet part 75 requirements and be available to demonstrate quantifiability and verifiability of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of valid operating hours for rate-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, only 'valid operating hours' (full or partial unit (or stack) operating hours for which (i) 'valid data' are obtained for all parameters used to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions (lbs) and (ii) the corresponding hourly gross energy output value is also valid data) count toward calculations. Substitute data from part 75, flow monitoring bias adjustments, and monitoring instruments that have not met required RAAT frequency are not 'valid data'. For operating hours with no useful output, zero is considered a valid value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and owners/operators must implement monitoring and QA procedures to ensure hours included in rate calculations meet this validity definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly CO2 mass emissions measurement and reporting for rate-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must measure and report hourly CO2 mass emissions (lbs) using procedures in paragraphs (a)(3)(i)-(vi): (i) install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a CO2 CEMS to directly measure and record CO2 concentrations and an exhaust gas flow rate monitoring system per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(i); as an alternative (if not using CCS) use certified O2 monitor per 75.10(a)(3)(iii) to calculate CO2 concentrations but account for non-combustion CO2 and ensure moisture monitoring if concentration measured on a dry basis; (ii) calculate hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/hr) per specified equations depending on wet/dry basis; (iii) convert to tons and then to lbs; (iv) record hourly tons/hr and operating times under 75.57(e) and report electronically under 75.64(a)(6) if required; (v) sum hourly CO2 mass emissions; (vi) ensure monitoring systems meet certification and QA procedures in 75.20 and appendices A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry contains stepwise measurement, conversion, recording, reporting, and QA/certification requirements; substitute data and certain bias-adjusted data are not 'valid.' Non-combustion CO2 sources must be accounted for when using O2 monitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative CO2 determination for units combusting only liquid and/or gaseous fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators that exclusively combust liquid and/or gaseous fuel may use alternative procedures: (i) implement procedures in appendix D to part 75 to determine hourly heat input using fuel flow and periodic GCV determinations with certified fuel flow meters; (ii) use Equation G-4 in appendix G to calculate hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/hr); (iii) multiply by operating time and convert tons to lbs; (iv) record and report hourly tons/hr and operating times per 75.57(e) and 75.64(a)(6) if required; (v) sum hourly CO2 mass emissions (lb); (vi) may determine site-specific carbon-based F-factors using Equation F-7b in appendix F and use them instead of default F_c in Equation G-4 nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternative path requires fuel flow meter QA and GCV determinations per appendix D and allows site-specific F-factors if properly calculated and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross energy output measurement (watt meters) and P_gross/net calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, owners/operators must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate sufficient watt meters to continuously measure and record hourly gross electric output using 0.2 accuracy class instrumentation and ANSI C12.20-2010 calibration. Combined heat and power (CHP) facilities must measure useful thermal and, if applicable, mechanical output. Procedures are specified to determine P_gross/net per hour, handle hours with no net electrical output, treat hours with zero output as valid for rate-based calculations, and calculate P_gross/net using equation terms (PE_ST, PE_CT, PE_IE, PE_A, PT_PS, PT_HR, PT_IE, TDF). For rate-based standards, sum P_gross/net for valid operating hours and divide total CO2 mass emissions for those hours by sum of P_gross/net to determine CO2 emissions rate (lb/MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes formulae for calculating useful thermal outputs (Pt_PS) and use of transmission and distribution factor (TDF) for CHP; special handling for hours with zero output and auxiliary loads; all terms must be in MWh and converted using operating time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common stack monitoring option
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs share a monitored common stack and are subject to the same emissions standard, the owner/operator may monitor the hourly CO2 mass emissions at the common stack in lieu of monitoring each EGU separately. If chosen, the hourly gross/net electric output for the common stack must be the sum of the hourly gross/net electric output of the individual EGUs and operating time must be expressed as 'stack operating hours' (per 40 CFR 72.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option requires aggregation of outputs and use of stack operating hours; consistency with § 60.13(g) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple stacks or ducts monitoring requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks (or routed to a common stack through multiple ducts and monitoring elected in the ducts), the hourly CO2 mass emissions and 'stack operating time' at each stack or duct must be monitored separately. Compliance must be determined by summing CO2 mass emissions measured at individual stacks/ducts and dividing by the gross or net energy output for the affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must monitor each emission path separately and aggregate results for compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment for EGUs serving a common electric generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, consistent with § 60.5775b, the combined hourly gross or net energy output must be apportioned to individual affected EGUs according to the fraction of the total steam load contributed by each EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and owners/operators must apply steam-load-based apportionment rules to attribute generation to individual units for rate calculations.
